explanation: `PFunctor.Obj α` is defined as the sigma type `Σ a : P.A, P.B a → α`, and `Obj.mk a f = ⟨a, f⟩`, `Obj.fst x = x.1`, `Obj.snd x = x.2` are all definitional. Hence the statement `Obj.mk x.fst x.snd = x` is definitionally the same as `Sigma.mk x.1 x.2 = x`, which is Mathlib's `Sigma.eta : ∀ x : Σ a, β a, Sigma.mk x.1 x.2 = x` instantiated at `α := P.A`, `β := P.B`. The library's own proof is `rfl`, i.e. it does not use `Sigma.eta`. (Note the `Obj.eta` name in Mathlib's PFunctor files is only the target theorem itself; no separate duplicate exists.)
